production_form: Household and kin production; farming household
period: First: before farming; farming household c. 12,000 years ago. Peak: until the rise of states
problem_solved: Provisioned people and passed on skill through reciprocity and obligation without money or command
cost_externalized: Unpaid household labor, mostly women's (T); under farming, soil, water and cleared commons (T)
organized_by: None found. Temple estates organized surplus; no evidence they arose to repair soil or commons
communications_tie: Speech and shared practice; Ronfeldt pairs speech and storytelling with tribes
operating_now: 16.4 billion hours of unpaid care work a day, 9% of global GDP (ILO 2018)

production_form: Privileged production: temple and palace estates, craft guilds, chartered companies
period: First: c. 3300 BCE estates (Uruk tablets, Metropolitan Museum of Art); guilds 1000 to 1880; East India Companies 1600 and 1602. Peak: guilds 13th to 17th c.; companies 17th to 18th c.
problem_solved: Scaled production by command and privilege; claimed trust in quality and skill training beyond kin (contested)
cost_externalized: Monopoly rents on consumers and exclusion of women and outsiders (E); colonized labor and land (T)
organized_by: Market form by capacity: hierarchy "cannot process complex exchanges" (Ronfeldt). No cost link found
communications_tie: Writing, then print; Ronfeldt pairs writing and printing with institutions (2025)
operating_now: Licensing, geographical indications, craft associations persist; no global figures gathered
node: Temple estate, guildhall and workshop, company warehouse
sources: Ogilvie 2008, 2019; Epstein; Ronfeldt 1996, 2025; Acemoglu, Johnson and Robinson 2005 (unread); Metropolitan Museum of Art

production_form: Factory, managerial corporation, global value chain
period: First: factory 1771 (Arkwright's Cromford Mill); corporation 1850s US; value chain late 20th c. Peak: now
problem_solved: Power and scale (factory); throughput coordination by managers (Chandler); coordination across borders (value chain)
cost_externalized: Child and adult labor (Factory Act 1833); air, rivers and sea (Alkali Act 1863); communities and distant sinks (T and E)
organized_by: Institutional form: factory inspectors (1833), Alkali Inspectorate (1863 to 1987), Clean Air Act (1956)
communications_tie: Power and transport (factory); railroad and telegraph (corporation, Chandler); internet (value chain). Ronfeldt pairs print, or telegraphy and telephony, with markets
node: Mill and factory, with stock exchange as capital node; data center as Market-owned infrastructure
sources: Factory Act 1833; RSC Environmental Chemistry Group; Science Museum; Chandler 1977; Ronfeldt 1996, 2025; Cromford Mills

production_form: Commons-based peer production; design global, manufacture local
period: First: GNU 1983; fab labs 2003; term 2002; DGML 2015. Peak: ahead, unknown
problem_solved: Matches people to creative tasks at near-zero cost; shares designs globally and fabricates locally
cost_externalized: Unpaid maintainer labor (60% unpaid, Tidelift 2024); energy and water through data centers (415 TWh in 2024, IEA); fabrication materials (unmeasured)
organized_by: None. No later form exists; founders cite proprietary restrictions and cheap computation
communications_tie: Networked information; matches Ronfeldt's network form
operating_now: OSS demand-side value US$8.8 trillion (disputed); 1,750 to 2,000+ fab labs (interested parties)
node: Fab lab, code repository, BioHub; place-based AI
sources: Benkler 2002, 2006; Stallman 1983, 1985; Kostakis et al. 2015; Hoffmann, Nagle and Zhou 2024; Whitacre 2024; Tidelift 2024; IEA 2025; Fab Foundation
